reason_invalid: Two independent, verified defects, either of which alone would invalidate the run: (1) the 'PVDAQ' telemetry used by the entire Gate 5.6 pipeline was synthetically generated inside the repository by rai/eval/external/solar/pvdaq.py::generate_pvdaq_telemetry(), not acquired from any real NREL PVDAQ / OEDI source, and this was not disclosed anywhere in the produced artifacts or documentation - the data was presented as real ('NREL PVDAQ provides high-fidelity, synchronized plane-of-array irradiance...') with real-sounding system IDs (SYS_10, SYS_34, SYS_4, SYS_1199, SYS_1283) and real facility names (NREL RSF, SERF, FSEC Cocoa). (2) The PVLIB_PHYSICS_REFERENCE model implementation (models.py::PVLibPhysicsReference.predict) used a formula that is line-for-line identical to the formula used inside generate_pvdaq_telemetry() to construct the synthetic 'actual' power (same temperature-derate term, same inverter-efficiency curve, same clipping ceiling), differing only by a small Gaussian noise term added at generation time. This means the physics model was validated against its own generating function, not independent data.
synthetic_data_evidence: rai/eval/external/solar/pvdaq.py (snapshotted copy in this directory) contains a function literally named generate_pvdaq_telemetry() that builds every telemetry column (ghi_wm2, poa_wm2, ambient_temp_c, module_temp_c, wind_speed_ms, dc_power_kw, ac_power_kw) from pvlib.solarposition + pvlib.location.Location.get_clearsky (Ineichen) + pvlib.irradiance.get_total_irradiance (Perez) + pvlib.temperature.sapm_cell + a hand-rolled Markov cloud-cover process + Gaussian noise, seeded by GATE56_SEED=20260912. scripts/gate56_solar_expected_performance.py called this function directly as its only data source. data/raw/ contained no pvdaq/ directory at audit time; no download manifest, no checksum, no source URL existed anywhere in the produced artifacts.
circular_validation_evidence: Formula-by-formula comparison of generate_pvdaq_telemetry() (lines ~327-341 of the snapshotted pvdaq.py) against PVLibPhysicsReference.predict() (lines 66-92 of the snapshotted models.py) shows: temp_derate = 1 + (temp_coefficient_pct_per_c/100)*(cell_temp-25) -> dc_power = rated_dc_kw*(poa/1000)*temp_derate [+/- small noise in the generator only] -> eff = inverter_efficiency_nominal*(1-0.02*(1-p_norm)**2) -> ac_power = min(dc_power*eff, rated_ac_kw). Both functions compute this identical chain. The physics reference model therefore recovers its own generating process, which mechanically explains the reported R^2 = 0.9994-0.9996 and nRMSE ~ 0.5% for that model regardless of whether real-world physics modeling works at all.
